subject: SCIENCE
title: Magnet Investigators
introduction: Milo tests a magnet with an iron nail and a wooden spoon. What will the magnet attract, and how can Maxine test it safely?

vocabulary.definition: An object that can attract some materials, such as iron or steel.
What an object is made of, such as iron, wood, or plastic.

activities.instruction: Watch Milo test magnetic materials and compare the poles safely.
activities.content: Magnets attract some materials, not all metals; poles can attract or repel. Use only an on-screen simulation or sealed adult-inspected magnet.

feedback.retry: Check the material and the poles: some metals attract, like poles repel, unlike poles attract.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: Magnets attract some materials, not all metals; poles can attract or repel. Use only an on-screen simulation or sealed adult-inspected magnet.

items.prompt: Milo tests an iron nail, a wooden spoon, and two magnet poles. Which statement is true?

options.text: Magnets attract some materials, not all metals; poles can attract or repel.
A magnet always pushes every object away.

items.explanation: Magnets attract some materials, such as iron, but not every metal or object. Depending on the poles, magnets can pull together or push apart.

items.prompt: Maxine holds a magnet near three objects. Which one might the magnet pull?
items.explanation: Iron is a material that magnets can attract strongly. Rubber, plastic, and wood are not usually pulled by a magnet.

items.prompt: Milo reads four magnet claims. Which one is NOT true?

options.text: An iron object may be attracted

items.explanation: Not all metals are magnetic; magnets attract particular materials such as iron. Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

items.prompt: Maxine brings two north poles close together. What should she predict?
items.explanation: Two north poles are like poles, so they push apart. Magnetism does not attract every object or all metals.

items.prompt: Milo turns one magnet around and brings unlike poles together. Which statement is true?

options.text: A magnet cannot affect another magnet

items.explanation: A north pole and a south pole are unlike poles, so they pull together. Wood is not normally attracted, and not all metals are magnetic.
